solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clever bit is to drink whisky

indicators.note: something that drinks takes a liquid inside itself, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a shred is a small bit or scrap
Whisky is the NATO alphabet code word for W

explanation.surface: A smart little trick: someone decides it would be clever to have a whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: SHREWD is SHRED with W swallowed between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd describes someone sharp and astute in judgement, a close synonym.

clue.text: Be quiet! Be quiet! Be quiet! That includes you at the back!

indicators.note: at the back points to the final letter only of the word just before it
the pair of hushing words holds the next piece within them

blocks.note: the usual two-letter call for silence
the same call for silence again

explanation.surface: A teacher losing patience, repeating the call for silence and pointing at the rowdy pupils in the back row.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Be quiet!' is the definition; the next two each give SH, and they enclose the U that ends 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shush is an interjection ordering someone to stop talking, exactly a demand for silence.

clue.text: Sort out unusual platform

indicators.note: to sort something out is to rearrange it, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone must fix a strange stage arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'Sort' is the fodder and 'out' the signal. Rum, meaning odd, is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand from which a speaker or conductor addresses people.

clue.text: Fine argument over wind installation

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means flipped so the letters run upward

blocks.note: OK means all right or fine
a row is a noisy quarrel
a vulgar word for breaking wind

explanation.surface: A fine quarrel breaks out over a wind turbine installation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' and 'wind' look like weather words; 'over' turns the first two pieces round together, and 'wind' is the vulgar sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An installation is a piece of gallery art, built in place, so it is one example of a creative piece.

clue.text: State of wordplay just as bad to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with asks for the opening letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: a pun is a piece of wordplay
first letters of just, as and bad

explanation.surface: A complaint that a state of punning is just as bad from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Punjab is a state of north-west India (and a province of Pakistan).
explanation.definitionFit: The Punjab is a federal state of India, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Vessel about to change course

indicators.note: a ship changing course alters its heading, so these letters alter their order

explanation.surface: A ship is about to turn onto a new heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'soon going to', but 'about' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German submarine, which is a kind of naval vessel.

clue.text: Start of year with rising rubbish? He'll clear it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upward, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: Jan 1, written JAN I, is the first day of the year

explanation.surface: New Year's Day brings mounting piles of rubbish, and someone is coming to clear them away.
explanation.walkthrough: The start of the year is not just JAN but Jan 1, with the 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor is a caretaker who cleans a building and tidies away mess.

clue.text: Support artist getting some breakfast

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A supporting artist on set gets some breakfast from catering.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon was a 20th-century British painter. Back bacon is the lean cut used in a British cooked breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Back bacon is a typical item served in a cooked breakfast, so it is some of that meal.

clue.text: Say why following pointer is not thorough

indicators.note: following places one part after the other in the line
say asks for the spoken form of the following word, written as a single letter

blocks.note: the arrow on a computer screen
the letter name is pronounced the same as the question word

explanation.surface: Asking why the pointer is skimpy, as if querying a sloppy diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursory means hasty and superficial, done without care for detail.

clue.text: My kind of moulding

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: Someone describing the sort of decorative moulding they like best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive, but it is the exclamation of surprise; cor is the British version.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is an ornamental band of plaster or stone running along the top of a wall.

clue.text: Thanks politician involved in study to reform tax

indicators.note: reforming something reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged
involved in means wrapped up inside, so the pair sits within the other word

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A grateful MP takes part in a review aimed at overhauling a tax.
explanation.walkthrough: Stamp duty is a UK tax paid on property purchases.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp duty is a levy charged by the British government, so it is one particular tax.

clue.text: Regulator's improper threat to incarcerate the majority

indicators.note: something improper is not in its correct form, so these letters are disordered
to incarcerate is to lock up inside, so one piece is shut within the other

explanation.surface: A regulatory body makes an improper threat to jail most of the population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regulator' looks like an official watchdog; here it is a device controlling temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat is a device that keeps heating at a set temperature by switching it on and off.

clue.text: On the way back, touch brass

indicators.note: heading back means travelling the other way, so the word is read right to left

blocks.note: to abut is to border on or touch

explanation.surface: On the way home, someone makes contact with brass, perhaps a doorknob or a rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' is the brass section of an orchestra; one instrument stands for the section.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the largest, lowest-pitched instrument of the orchestral brass family.

clue.text: A hundred bullets ricocheted,

indicators.note: a ricochet bounces back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred rounds bounced off a wall, and the sentence stops mid-breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the punctuation mark that ends the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed mark at the end of the clue is itself an example of this punctuation sign.

clue.text: Woman's heart in the beginning of it all, and the end for some

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
in places the selected letter inside the following phrase's word

blocks.note: the Creation is the start of the world

explanation.surface: A woman's heart is present from the start of everything to the end of some lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The Creation, the beginning of everything, takes in the M at the centre of 'woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremation is a common way of disposing of the dead, the final stage of life for some people.

clue.text: Jagger, say, welcomed as a nonconformist

indicators.note: welcomed means taken in, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: Mick Jagger of the Rolling Stones
to aver is to state or say

explanation.surface: Mick Jagger, as an example, being welcomed as a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is the verb meaning state.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an independent-minded person who refuses to follow the crowd.

clue.text: Wild raves after debauchery? The other way round

indicators.note: after puts the second part behind the first in the line
something wild is out of control, so these letters run in a disordered way

blocks.note: vice is immoral or depraved behaviour

explanation.surface: Wild parties following an orgy, or perhaps the orgy came after the parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Wild raves are written first but come second: the debauchery leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is a Latin phrase meaning with the order or positions reversed.

clue.text: What tyre can be indeed

indicators.note: in places the state of the tyre inside the following word

explanation.surface: A remark about a punctured tyre: it can indeed go flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' looks like emphasis, but it splits into 'in deed'. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre that has lost its air is let down, which is exactly the condition of being emptied of air.

clue.text: Small rise in fat downwind

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rise reads from the bottom upward, so the word runs backwards
in puts the turned word inside the next one

blocks.note: wee is Scottish and informal British for small

explanation.surface: A dieter notices a slight increase in body fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward is the side sheltered from the wind, facing the direction it blows toward.

clue.text: Gangster hiding ale? That's chicken

indicators.note: hiding letters puts them out of sight, so they are removed from the name

explanation.surface: A gangster stashing beer is accused of cowardice.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, L and E from AL CAPONE (AL from the front, E from the end) to leave CAPON. 'chicken' looks like coward; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, a particular kind of fowl.

clue.text: Start to tuck into Spanish dish to find a bone

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word
into places that letter inside the dish

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a paella and finds a bone in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' reads as eat heartily, but 'into' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, a small bone at the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Prison coverage not over

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the word that follows from the longer word

explanation.surface: Media coverage of a jail story is still running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not over' looks like 'still going', but it removes the four letters of over from coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage confines someone like a cell does, so it is used loosely for a jail.

clue.text: Proposal includes one barrel as incentive

indicators.note: includes means one word holds the others within it

blocks.note: a motion is a formal proposal at a meeting
I is the Roman numeral one
a vat is a large tub or barrel

explanation.surface: A business proposal offers a barrel as a reward to tempt people in.
explanation.definitionFit: Motivation is the drive or reason that spurs someone to act, much like a spur or inducement.

clue.text: Communist not a wet

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the following letter from the word

explanation.surface: A political jibe: this communist is not a wet, a feeble moderate.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a wet is a moderate Conservative; here 'wet' is just the adjective for damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly damp, so it is a mild synonym for being soaked with liquid.

clue.text: One out of six is sheepish

indicators.note: out of here means placed on the outside of the next word, wrapping round it

blocks.note: VI is the Roman numeral six

explanation.surface: One in six people looks embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One out of six' reads as a fraction; here it means the word one goes outside the numeral. 'sheepish' is taken literally, not as embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means relating to or resembling sheep, the literal sense of a sheep-like adjective.

clue.text: Some thought it a nice ship

indicators.note: some means only a part of the words that follow is wanted

explanation.surface: Some people thought it a lovely vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship's name runs across thoughT IT A NICe. The surface wryly recalls the famous liner people admired before it sank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic was the White Star liner that sank on its maiden voyage in 1912.

clue.text: Distillery discarding DIY dodgy framework

indicators.note: discarding throws away those letters from the longer word
something dodgy is unreliable or out of order, so the letters left are jumbled

explanation.surface: A distillery gives up on some shoddy home-made frame.
explanation.walkthrough: Take D, I and Y from DISTILLERY to leave STILLER, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice of wooden or metal strips on which climbing plants are trained.

clue.text: Modern song on the radio lacking coverage

indicators.note: on the radio means as broadcast and heard, not as written

blocks.note: a modern song is a new ditty

explanation.surface: A new song is played on air but gets no media attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking coverage' looks like the song's poor press; it means wearing no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudity is the state of having no clothes on, the body being left bare.

clue.text: Starter is able to mimic

explanation.surface: A beginner can copy others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a beginner; it is a small savoury served before a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small bite of bread or pastry with a topping, served as an appetiser.
